title: Install Entra Policy Suite 2.0 in your own Azure subscription
purpose: Creates Entra Policy Suite in one resource group of your subscription - managed identities, Log Analytics, a container registry with the engine image built in it, Azure SQL (Entra-only), a Container Apps environment and the jobs - and grants the engine identity the Graph and Exchange rights it needs and the tick identity only the right to send to the job queues and pull its image. Every feature is off afterwards.
whenToRun: Once, to install. Again with the same parameters to resume an install that stopped.

runAs.name: Owner
runAs.why: creates the resource group and resources and the role assignments

runAs.name: Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: grants the engine identity Graph and Exchange app roles and the Exchange Recipient Administrator role; creates the web sign-in registration and gives its admin consent

changes.object: resource group (default rg-eps) with: 2 user-assigned managed identities (id-eps-engine - also the scheduler, id-eps-web), Log Analytics workspace log-eps, container registry acreps<suffix> (Basic), Azure SQL server sql-eps-<suffix> (Entra-only, you as admin) + database eps (S0), Container Apps environment cae-eps, jobs caj-eps-tick (every 5 min) + one job per work job, each started from its own queue (caj-eps-usertag, caj-eps-devicetag, ..., caj-eps-uplink - the Invardia telemetry every 4 h)
changes.why: where Entra Policy Suite runs

changes.object: firewall rule AllowAllWindowsAzureIps on the SQL server, and a temporary AllowSetupHost rule for the machine running the install (removed again at the end of the SQL step)
changes.why: the jobs reach SQL from Azure; the installer applies the schema

changes.object: id-eps-engine and id-eps-web
changes.why: the jobs and the web app pull the image

changes.object: custom role 'EntraPolicySuite job starter (<resource group>)' and its assignment to the scheduler's identity, if an older install made them
changes.why: the tick holds no right to start jobs (the jobs start from their own queues)

changes.object: an older install's separate scheduler identity id-eps-tick: its role assignments, its database user and the identity, each read back - only after verify has run the scheduler as id-eps-engine
changes.why: the scheduler runs as the engine identity (the same model in every product)

changes.object: storage account steps<suffix> (no shared key, TLS 1.2) + one queue per work job
changes.why: the tick asks for a job run by a message on the job's queue; the job is started by its queue

changes.object: id-eps-engine (the scheduler runs as the engine)
changes.why: the scheduler asks for a job run by putting a message on that job's queue

changes.object: id-eps-engine
changes.permission: Storage Queue Data Message Processor + Storage Queue Data Reader
changes.why: a job takes and deletes its message; the queue trigger counts the messages as the engine identity

changes.object: id-eps-engine
changes.permission: Microsoft Graph application: User.ReadWrite.All, Device.ReadWrite.All, GroupMember.Read.All, Organization.Read.All, AuditLog.Read.All, Policy.Read.All (read only), RoleManagement.Read.Directory (read only), DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All (read only: the identity report's Intune devices), Application.Read.All (read only), Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess (the stage buttons only)
changes.why: write the tags on users and devices, read group members and licences for the rules, read the audit log to say who changed a watched tag (the tamper monitor), read application names for the CA documentation (Application.Read.All), and move ONE adopted Conditional Access policy ONE stage when a SuperAdmin asks for it, after he saw the change (Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess; leave it out with -ExcludeGraphRole Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess and the stage buttons are refused by the tenant)
changes.undo: remove the app role assignments of id-eps-engine

changes.object: id-eps-engine
changes.permission: Office 365 Exchange Online application: Exchange.ManageAsApp + the Entra role Exchange Recipient Administrator
changes.why: read Exchange recipient types for the rules and the identity report, and write a mail-enabled user's custom attribute when Graph refuses it - only while user tagging, the identity report or a rule with a mailbox condition is on; a run while none of them is on removes it
changes.undo: remove the app role assignment and the role assignment

changes.object: app registration 'Entra Policy Suite' + its enterprise application: single tenant, code flow only (no implicit grant), no groups claim, NO secret and NO certificate; its own delegated scope api://<app id>/user_impersonation; assignment required, you assigned; a federated credential for id-eps-web
changes.permission: admin consent: Microsoft Graph delegated openid, profile, offline_access, User.Read; the app's own user_impersonation to itself
changes.why: the shared sign-in front signs people in to the web app with it (the web identity is its client credential - no secret)

changes.object: Key Vault kv-eps-<suffix> (Standard, RBAC, soft delete 90 days, purge protection) with one RSA key 'signin-front' (wrap / unwrap only); the install stores no secret there (Invardia may add one: the per-install telemetry key 'uplink-key')
changes.why: the sign-in front wraps the keys that protect its sessions with it
changes.undo: delete the vault (it stays recoverable for 90 days - purge protection)

changes.object: id-eps-web
changes.permission: Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User
changes.why: the sign-in front wraps and unwraps its keys

changes.object: id-eps-engine
changes.scope: the secret 'uplink-key' only - granted only when that secret exists; the install never creates the secret or reads its value
changes.why: the uplink job reads the per-install key Invardia issued, at send time, to report to Invardia (identified only: without the key nothing is sent)

changes.object: Container App ca-eps-web: the sign-in front (signin-front:<pinned version>, built in the registry from the release's source) on the public HTTPS ingress, the GUI (the engine image, EPS_JOB = Web) on 127.0.0.1 behind it, as id-eps-web; scale 0-1; never Easy Auth
changes.why: the web app

changes.object: schema signin owned by id-eps-web + CREATE TABLE (the front's two state tables); you as the web app's first SuperAdmin in eps.WebAccess (audited)
changes.why: the sign-in front keeps its sessions there; someone must be able to grant access in the app
changes.undo: drop the schema; remove the access row

changes.object: PRIVATE install only (-PrivateNetwork): the network vnet-eps (default 10.230.0.0/24) with snet-eps-apps (delegated to Microsoft.App/environments) and snet-eps-endpoints - or, with -VnetId, only a missing subnet in your network and the delegation of an empty apps subnet
changes.scope: the resource group, or your network
changes.why: the Container Apps environment and the private endpoints live in it
changes.undo: delete the network / the subnets and the delegation

changes.object: PRIVATE install only: the privatelink DNS zones (database, vaultcore, queue, azurecr) linked to the network - or, with -PrivateDnsZonesResourceGroupId, your zones used and nothing written there; the environment's own zone (@, *, *.internal); one private endpoint each for Azure SQL, Key Vault, the job queues and the registry (Premium) with their DNS records; the registry's build pool epspool; Azure SQL, Key Vault, the storage account and the registry created with public network access Disabled (no firewall rule, no exception); the Container Apps environment cae-eps-vnet, internal (no public address); a one-time job caj-eps-insidecheck (deleted after it ran)
changes.why: nothing of the install is reachable from the internet; the inside check proves it works from inside the network

changes.object: PRIVATE install, only with -PeerToHub / -LinkZonesToHub and only when your rights allow it (checked first): the peering spoke <-> hub (both sides, never half) and the install's zones linked to the hub
changes.scope: the spoke and the hub network
changes.why: your clients and the hybrid worker reach the web app and the names resolve through the hub
changes.undo: delete the peerings and the zone links

changes.object: PUBLIC -> PRIVATE only: the old environment cae-eps (after the inside check; its jobs and web app re-created in cae-eps-vnet), its address in the web sign-in registration; public network access then Disabled on SQL (its public firewall rules removed), Key Vault, storage and the registry
changes.why: a Container Apps environment cannot move into a network
changes.undo: run the install again without -PrivateNetwork in a new resource group

changes.object: PRIVATE install: network-hand-off.txt and, with -HubVnetId, prepare-hub-entrapolicysuite.ps1 in the state folder
changes.why: the exact list for your network team, and a script the hub owner can read and run

changes.object: the eps schema; the roles eps_engine, eps_tick, eps_web, eps_worker with object-level grants from sql/eps-grants.json (no db_datareader / db_datawriter); the database users id-eps-engine (roles eps_engine and eps_tick - it is also the scheduler) and id-eps-web (eps_web)
changes.permission: per role: SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE on named tables only (the audit trail INSERT + SELECT only)
changes.why: each part reads and writes only its own data (least privilege)
changes.undo: drop the users and roles / delete the database

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: the resource group (an install made before 2.0.55: rg-entrapolicysuite, found by itself when it is there)

parameters.name: PrivateNetwork
parameters.help: install into your virtual network (no public address; private endpoints)

parameters.name: VnetId
parameters.help: your existing network (resource id); empty = the install makes vnet-eps

parameters.name: VnetAddressPrefix
parameters.help: the range of the network the install makes (at least /25)

parameters.name: VnetName
parameters.help: the name of the network the install makes

parameters.name: AppsSubnetPrefix
parameters.help: its range when it is created (default the first /26)

parameters.name: EndpointsSubnetPrefix
parameters.help: its range when it is created (default the second /26)

parameters.name: PrivateDnsZonesResourceGroupId
parameters.help: your central private DNS zones (used, never written)

parameters.name: HubVnetId
parameters.help: your hub network (for the hand-off list and the hub owner's script)

parameters.name: PeerToHub
parameters.help: peer with the hub, both sides, when your rights allow it

parameters.name: LinkZonesToHub
parameters.help: link the install's zones to the hub when your rights allow it

parameters.name: ConfirmedFromInside
parameters.help: you checked a private install's web app from inside your network yourself

readsOnly: the subscription and its resource providers
the tenant's Graph and Exchange service principals
network: private install: <registry>.azurecr.io and <registry>.<region>.data.azurecr.io, <server>.database.windows.net through their private endpoints - run it from a machine inside your network
whatIf: Every step, what exists and what it would create - nothing is created, registered or granted.
undo: Delete the resource group, and the engine identity's app role and Exchange role assignments (they go with the identity when the resource group is deleted).
